notes: Internet-company monetization and valuation subepisode; analyzed in the shared dot-com/telecom cluster rather than counted as an independent crisis. QQQ begins only in 1999, so earlier market context requires a Nasdaq Composite series.

Fiber and carrier-capacity subepisode; shares the same statistical cluster as internet speculation because demand and financing pathways overlap. Exact rollover dates remain target-generation inputs, not fitted labels.
Objective target dates must be regenerated from archived Census and financing releases; these dates define audit windows, not fitted labels.
Commodity-market recognition can precede the final economic rollover; sequence is intentionally not forced to be monotonic.
Final rollover label must be generated from archived rigs, drilling, production and filing evidence.
Same-family control: investment and activity expanded without a predeclared material economic rollover before the control window ended.
Cross-family control: hyperscaler investment expanded through the window without a predeclared broad capacity rollover.

Semiconductor and electronic-equipment production pathway within the shared dot-com/telecom cluster; it is not counted as an independent crisis from the internet and telecom subepisodes. Objective dates must be generated from archived G.17 releases.
Same-family expansion control for the semiconductor production and utilization rule.
Pre-pandemic semiconductor inventory-cycle correction; window ends before the March 2020 shutdown shock. Objective dates must be generated from archived G.17 releases.
Post-shortage semiconductor capacity and inventory unwind. Objective dates must be generated from archived G.17 releases rather than assigned from equity hindsight.
Producer-side oil shock after supply outran demand; objective dates must be generated from archived STEO releases and this episode remains in the shale-2014 shared statistical cluster.
Same-family oil-market control bounded before the pandemic; used to falsify price and physical-balance shock rules.

Consumer-side price and supply-buffer shock spanning the post-pandemic demand recovery and 2022 geopolitical disruption; the mechanisms must be reported separately rather than attributed to one cause.
Historical holdout for the consumer-upside oil squeeze rule frozen after the 2014-2023 development sample; the global financial crisis is a major confound and the episode is not prospective evidence.
